source_refs.evidence: Workflow.inputs independently loads rules/config before Sources.capture, forbids source_versions keys beginning rules:, then extends those rule versions and prepends the returned rule text. A new committed-object WorkflowSources implementation cannot replace this producer through the current source port.
load_rules reads project.config_ref and rule_refs from the live Project root, hashes those bytes, applies config.with_project_text, and returns the exact text inserted into the model Context.
The initial initialize/prepare_pack calls both pass through this separate live producer; this is an initial Context consumer, not merely a future later-phase integration.

Full reservation/source CAS sees a consistent live rules hash, so cannot restore the promised same-commit origin. The existing design already requires tracked rules/config from the same commit; section10.1 names object capture but leaves its actual independent rule/config ingress unspecified. This is a finite initial input composition gap, not a request to finish all Sources/Gates/CLI or add a new rule policy.

verified_design_properties.property: The bootstrap breaks the initial Context/Git admission cycle without inventing Agent work or an accepted artifact.
verified_design_properties.rationale: The existing allocator registers the ExecutionUnit/Task projection before registered base resolution and worktree creation. UnitGit records helper intent under current authority before spawn and bounds its wait/receipt. Workflow initialize reads a Task snapshot before asynchronous inputs and later persists by CAS; placing initial registration before that snapshot avoids a self-created version conflict. The design explicitly requires committed tree/blob reads through a new production source port, Preparing with no Session/work/artifact, and no fabricated successful result.

verified_design_properties.property: Adoption is a private producer-proven operation with exact atomic authority rather than reconstruction from a row.
verified_design_properties.rationale: The proposed non-Clone, non-serializable capability must be returned by the successful preparation producer and retain the existing abandonment guard beyond the current tuple-return boundary. The adoption transaction explicitly checks unit/version/epoch/generation, active Task projection, prepared namespace/base/provider/profile, permissions and no Session/work/artifact/native input/quota/unresolved helper. It shares the concrete Workflow/Context/owner CAS checks already used for reservation. Only phase and history unit binding change; generation/resource identity remain stable. Failed adoption rolls back both writes, and capability abandonment retires only its owned unit. This is feasible as a separate producer/API and is not satisfied by simply wrapping an arbitrary recovered ExecutionUnit.

verified_design_properties.property: The first real phase follows actual Workflow ordering while later attempts keep fresh namespaces and retained result provenance.
verified_design_properties.rationale: Quick starts Worktree then Implement; Standard/Strict begin Issue, Worktree, Requirements. Initial evidence success is separate from Agent success and does not create a retained artifact. Subsequent Executor phases remain genuinely fresh attempts consuming retained accepted revisions; readonly reviewer/verifier input authorities stay separate. No conflicting generation advance or obligatory fabricated initial artifact is required by this contract.

verified_design_properties.property: The reserved preparation mode has actual consumer grant restrictions and an explicit old-writer migration boundary.
verified_design_properties.rationale: Current native start performs a registered version probe before Session insertion, so the proposed refusal must precede that probe as stated; transaction-local Session rejection is an independent second guard. Ordinary public preparation must reject the reserved phase. Existing guards use connection-local contract 4 on all listed mutable tables and initialization checks the maximum schema. Atomically replacing the guards with contract 5 and increasing the supported schema can reject already-open contract-4 writers and old-binary reopening without changing execution table layout or minting preparation provenance. The ordered upgrade must install compatible current guards before any data write requiring the new contract; actual migration behavior remains to be implemented and tested.
